card.summary: Unbounded. `max_upload_size` defaults to 50M and can be set to any value; storage and media retention are entirely operator-controlled.

free_tier.stated: Unbounded. `max_upload_size` defaults to 50M and can be set to any value; storage and media retention are entirely operator-controlled.

egress.terms: Bandwidth depends on host server allocation. Fronting endpoints with caching CDNs allows media caching to reduce origin egress traffic.

record.tooling: Synapse (Python) or Dendrite/Conduit; standard Matrix media API so rclone's `s3`/`webdav`-adjacent tooling plus any Matrix SDK works. Admin media API allows listing and purging media per user/room.
record.chaining: Not a free provider. The multiplier angle is that media is content-addressed and deduplicated by Synapse, and federation lets you push copies to other homeservers as a second replica.
record.limits_note: `max_upload_size` default 50M; reverse proxy must be raised too (nginx default body size bites first). `media_retention.local_media_lifetime` / `remote_media_lifetime` can silently delete anything not accessed within the window.
record.reliability_note: Default installs are safe; the risk is operator misconfiguration. Enabling media_retention turns the repo into a TTL cache. Federation media cache is the first thing purged.

evidence.proved: 'max_upload_size — The largest allowed upload size in bytes... Defaults to 50M.'
'media_retention ... control whether media will be purged if it has not been accessed in a given amount of time'
